_comment: Voice casting for The Lamplight Cipher. Every voice is a British-accented ElevenLabs voice chosen against the character's description in story-bible.json — the setting is a 1998 coastal English pilotage authority, so an American read would break the world instantly. 'why' records the casting reasoning so a future recast can be judged against intent rather than taste.

wren.why: Wren is nineteen with flat Ilberry vowels and no charm. A Midlands read gives the regional flatness the bible insists on, and keeps her from sounding like a BBC narrator — she is the one person here who is not performing.

sabine-ferrier-kyne.why: The Warden's weapon is unhurried courtesy. A refined, seasoned older voice lets every line be perfectly pleasant and still land wrong on a second listen, which is exactly how the character works.

halvard-pike.why: Forty-four years a clerk and every one of them a grievance. An older, professional, slightly dry read carries contempt without shouting — Pike's disgust is procedural, not emotional.

ottoline-verge.why: Seventy-two, unpaid, and delighted to be asked. Warm and grandmotherly, because the horror of Ottoline is that she hands the player the murder weapon — the p.p. convention — as a friendly item of housekeeping.

enid-charnock.why: Cashier since 1962, and the reason the truth survives is her refusal to throw away a used ribbon spool. Clear, precise, unornamented — a woman who reads out a figure the same way whether it is fourpence or thirty-one lives.

rita-tain.why: Boatwoman and lamp-room curator who has spent twenty-four years and every penny she owns being right and unable to prove it. A warm, natural, working coastal voice — not genteel, not institutional.

phyllida-halkett.why: Exists to explain section 41 procedure at exhausting length and to refuse, every single time, to have an opinion. A flat professional register is the joke and the integrity at once.

ivo-sandbach.why: A conservation architect whose site diary is an accidental alibi ledger. Calm, measured, faintly pleased with his own thoroughness.

bram-aylward.why: Introduces himself as a Ministry liaison, which is the first thing he says and the first thing that is not true. A pleasant voice with something slightly off in it does more than a sinister one.

marren-iveson.why: Two officers, one car, and no appetite for an archivist's theory. Calm, unhurried, faintly tired — a working detective, not a TV one.

cormac-sallow.why: Seventy-nine, dead before the game begins, heard only through his own letters. An old seafaring voice makes the readings feel like a recording of someone who was really there — which is the whole point of him.

narrator.why: Cinematic narration only. Deep and calm, so the cold open sounds like weather rather than a trailer.
